recommended_title: How Far Do k Benchmarks Go? Cold-Start Benchmark Selection and Score Imputation on Family-Disjoint Held-Out Models
central_question: When only k benchmarks can be run on a new model, how accurately can a history-fitted selector-plus-imputer recover its scores on the remaining benchmarks, how does that error fall with k, and how much of the gain comes from cross-benchmark structure versus the choice of which k to run?
central_thesis: On three public leaderboards (MTEB, Open LLM Leaderboard, HELM Lite) with family-disjoint held-out models, a wrapper-selected, rank-Gauss-transformed, NNLS-stacked Gaussian imputer cuts held-out error substantially relative to column-mean imputation (final qualified outcome; skill 0.434, nRMSE 0.562) and beats permuted-observation controls by a wide margin, but its edge over random-k selection with a ridge imputer is small (0.016), error falls only with diminishing returns in k (MTEB nRMSE 0.787 at k=2 to 0.638 at k=20), and difficulty differs by leaderboard.
narrative_rationale: The sealed final evaluation completed with outcome qualified (final.qualification.outcome = qualified, status = completed, correct = true), so the paper can report measured results as a positive-but-modest finding. The strongest defensible story is a calibrated empirical characterization of the cold-start budget question: (i) cross-benchmark structure is real and exploitable (large gain over column mean, large permuted-control gap), (ii) the marginal value of choosing the subset cleverly versus randomly is small in this regime, and (iii) error vs k shows diminishing returns on MTEB. This answers the task's 'how large must k be' question with an error-vs-k curve rather than a threshold, and avoids overclaiming selection or a mechanism: the evaluator reports selector+imputer jointly, no ablation separating selection from imputation produced numbers (ablation_studies is empty, offline experiment scripts were not executed in the evidence), no theory check results exist, and candidate diagnostics are marked unverified. Thesis-first organization (question, protocol, method, error-vs-k, baselines/controls, per-leaderboard difficulty, limitations) beats discovery order. No downstream_study block exists in paper_data.json; the search stage (three model variants, all scored) is used only as a small, clearly labelled search-partition comparison on the MTEB search split, kept separate from the sealed final results.
edit_framing_decision: Not in edit mode: no previous_paper or staged inputs exist. Fresh framing; nothing from a prior manuscript is preserved or rejected beyond this default.
staged_input_impact: No staged paper, program, or edit context is present; framing is derived only from paper_data.json (final_evaluation, search-stage program records), the task contract/evaluators, and the candidate source files.

method_groups.name: Wrapper-selected, rank-Gauss stacked Gaussian imputer (selected configuration)
method_groups.include_reason: The studied method (best search score; best_correct = c02). Components: rank-Gauss or z-score representation, EM Gaussian with missing entries, benchmark selection from covariance-trace greedy and K-fold held-out-error wrapper forward selection (choice by history-only CV), per-target NNLS stack of Gaussian conditional means at several shrinkages, ridge on selected benchmarks, kNN over history models and column median, range clipping, median-shrink fallback. Described from the source file; every tuned quantity uses history rows only.

method_groups.name: Greedy conditional-variance selection with Gaussian conditional-mean imputation
method_groups.include_reason: First model variant; the only grounded comparison to the selected one under the search protocol (search nRMSE 1.067 vs 1.028; skill vs random 0.100 vs 0.132; permuted gap 0.522 vs 0.568). Differences confound transform, selector, stacking and clipping, so it must be presented as a variant comparison, not a component ablation.

method_groups.name: Monotone latent-skill member plus A-optimal latent selector added to the stack
method_groups.include_reason: Third variant; its search metrics and per-seed scores are identical to the selected one (combined 0.2467, both seeds), i.e. no measurable gain. Report as a null result. Cause (member not retained by CV, vs. no effect) is unknown from the artifacts; state that.

method_groups.name: Evaluator baselines and controls: column-mean imputation, random-k ridge, greedy-forward-selection ridge, permuted and constant-observation controls
method_groups.include_reason: These define skill (1 - candidate nRMSE / baseline nRMSE, clipped to [-1,1]) and the permuted-control gap; they ground the 0.434 / 0.016 / 0.099 / 0.678 numbers. Only the aggregated values are available, not per-baseline nRMSE.

results_focus: Error-vs-k on MTEB (final): nRMSE 0.787 (k=2), 0.722 (k=5), 0.664 (k=10), 0.638 (k=20); monotone with diminishing returns; this is the direct answer to 'how large a k'. Only four k values and a single curve; no baseline curve is available, so do not claim a 'sufficient k' threshold.

Per-leaderboard sealed-final nRMSE: MTEB 0.703, HELM Lite 0.501, Open LLM Leaderboard 0.482, pooled 0.562 (equal weights across seeds, k grid and families). State that k grids and column counts differ by family (MTEB k in {2,5,10,20} of 297 columns; OLL k in {1,2,3} of 6 columns; HELM k in {2,3,5} of 10 columns), so cross-family differences are not a pure difficulty ranking.

Skill against baselines (final, pooled): vs column-mean 0.434 (three seed episodes 0.433, 0.427, 0.433), vs greedy-forward ridge 0.099, vs random-k ridge 0.016. Lead with the honest reading: large gain over history-only, modest over ridge, marginal over random selection; selector and imputer are evaluated jointly, so the 0.016 cannot be attributed to selection alone.
Negative-control evidence: permuted-observation control gap 0.678 (control nRMSE minus real nRMSE, pooled), supporting that gains come from cross-benchmark information in the observed scores.

Search-partition variant comparison (MTEB search split only, two seeds each): c01 0.2199 / nRMSE 1.067; c02 0.2467 / 1.028; c03 0.2467 / 1.028 (identical to c02). Keep clearly separate from sealed final results; skill-vs-mean on search is combined_score internally, present it as skill vs column mean.

Scope and limitations as a results view: held-out models are family-group-disjoint (>=25% of groups by hash order, OLL capped at 300 held-out rows); non-adaptive selection committed before any new-model score; three seeds (201-203); candidate diagnostics unverified; no confidence intervals for pooled metrics beyond seed-level final-score episodes; scores differ in meaning across leaderboards.
figure_plan: Fig. 1 (overview, page 1-2): cold-start protocol schematic: history matrix with missing cells -> commit k columns (non-adaptive) -> observe k scores of held-out model -> imputer -> predictions on remaining N-k columns scored in column-std units; with a side strip naming the three leaderboards and the baselines/controls.

Fig. 2 (main results, 3 panels, full width): (a) MTEB nRMSE vs k; (b) per-leaderboard and pooled final nRMSE; (c) pooled skill against column-mean, greedy-ridge, random-k ridge. Only grounded numbers; no invented error bars (use seed-episode points only where seed values exist, i.e. final skill vs column mean).

figure_specs.layout_rationale: ICLR template is single-column (text width about 5.5 in); a left-to-right protocol diagram with 5 labelled stages needs full text width for legible 8-9 pt labels; place on page 1 or 2.

supplementary_plan.purpose: Give the reader what is needed to reimplement and audit the study without placing evidence essential to the thesis out of the body: full method specification, evaluator protocol details, and per-metric tables.

notes_for_writer: Final outcome is qualified (final.qualification.outcome=qualified, status=completed, correct=true). Say so plainly; it reflects the evaluator's gates (positive skill vs column mean and vs random-k, controls worse than real), not generalization beyond the three leaderboards. Do not invent gate diagnostics beyond that.

No downstream_study section exists. Do not claim a 'frozen selection' study; state that the studied method is the best-scoring search variant (c02; c03 tied exactly) and that all three search attempts were scored. Which tied variant the final evaluator ran is not stated in paper_data; do not assert it beyond best_correct = c02 and the final program tree hash.

Reader-facing metric names: 'normalized RMSE (nRMSE, in historical column-std units, equal weight per held-out model)'; 'skill vs baseline B = 1 - nRMSE_candidate / nRMSE_B (clipped to [-1,1])'; 'permuted-control gap'. Rename final_score as 'skill vs column-mean imputation'. Use 'model variant', 'seeded run', 'configuration' per the presentation contract.

Selector and imputer are scored jointly. The evaluator's random-k and greedy baselines use ridge-style imputation (and column-mean for skill_mean), so skill vs random-k ridge mixes selection and imputer differences. Do not credit the 0.016 or 0.099 to the selection rule. Phrase the finding as 'the end-to-end pipeline beats ...'.

Quantities NOT available (never invent): per-baseline nRMSE values, per-family skill, per-k baselines, confidence intervals on pooled metrics, per-seed values for metrics other than final score, results of offline ablation/theory scripts (experiments.py was not executed within the evidence), search-partition baselines other than the three listed metrics. A relative gain over random-k of 1.6% from three seeds is stated without a significance claim.

Cross-leaderboard comparison caveat: OLL has 6 columns (k up to 3 means half of all columns observed), HELM 10 columns, MTEB 297; k grids differ; pooled nRMSE averages these with equal family weight. Say difficulty ordering is confounded by N and k.

Search nRMSE exceeds 1 on the search split (1.067, 1.028) while final pooled nRMSE is 0.562; these are different partitions and aggregation, so do not compare them directly; explain without speculating on cause (cause unknown).

Search-stage table: present as a three-row 'model-variant comparison on the MTEB search split' with two seeds; avoid chronology words (cycle, iteration, then). Note c03 is identical to c02 to all reported digits (a null result for latent-skill member and A-optimal selector) and its cause is not identified.

Related work must cite only references that exist in references.bib and are relevant: SubLIME (Saranathan2025SubLIMESS), SimBA (Subramani2025SimBASB), From Benchmarks to Skills (Maimon2025FromBT), Mapping Overlaps in Benchmarks (Wu2025MappingOI). The bib also contains many irrelevant retrieved entries (LoRA, medical, etc.); do not cite them. Starter-literature papers (MTEB, HELM, tinyBenchmarks, metabench, BenchBench, observational scaling laws, Sloth) are not in references.bib; cite them only if added to the bib with verified entries, otherwise describe the gap in related work without a citation key.

Theoretical content: none grounded. The venue asks for mechanistic motivation; supply only the standard conditional-Gaussian/A-optimal rationale for why conditional variance or held-out-error selection should help, labelled as motivation, not as a verified mechanism. State that the planned synthetic theory check has no reported numbers.

Page budget (8-9 body pages, single column): spend space on (1) a precise problem formulation and protocol, (2) a reimplementable method section, (3) results with the two figures plus a compact metric table and the variant table, (4) a substantive limitations section (joint scoring, three seeds, three leaderboards, embedding vs LLM leaderboards, non-adaptive selection, unverified diagnostics, missing ablations), (5) discussion on practitioner implications (what k buys, when random-k is nearly as good). No padding; if evidence is short, tighten rather than add unsupported claims.

Layout: ICLR single-column; both required figures at full text width (target_width_fraction 1.0). Overview figure on page 1-2 via generate-concept-figure; main_results via matplotlib exporting PDF and 300-DPI PNG, PDF referenced in LaTeX; raster fallback must be >=2400 px wide, never upscaled.
Venue: double-blind, no authors or links; include LLM Usage section (may be in appendix); calibrated claims, no SOTA language.

Dataset caveat: MTEB models are text-embedding models and tasks are embedding tasks, not generative LLM benchmarks; the title/abstract should say 'models' and name the leaderboards rather than implying LLM-wide generality. OLL and HELM are LLM leaderboards.
